Hi Priya — thanks for the documents. Quick note on our side:

- We put the payment on hold because our payment ops saw mixed jurisdictional evidence (SG GST + India GST) and our collector flow defaulted to APAC withholding for marketplace transactions when country of supplier != billing entity.

- Two paths to clear the hold quickly:
  1) Split the invoice so that Redwood Asia Pte Ltd invoices the SG portion (no India withholding) and Redwood India Pvt Ltd invoices the India-resident portion (reverse-charge / local GST handling). That requires a simple invoice allocation matrix from you (line-level revenue allocation).
  2) If CloudPoint prefers a single invoice, we need a signed affidavit (DocuSign) from CloudPoint confirming tax residency and that you accept reverse-charge handling for services supplied to Redwood. Finance will then validate VAT/GST IDs and release payment.

Ive attached a draft allocation matrix (proposed-split-invoice-matrix.xlsx) and started a DocuSign envelope for the affidavit (rdw-apac-affidavit-docusign.pdf). Marissa from Finance is on copy to confirm the exact document list required for release.

Suggested next step: Priya, can you confirm which path you prefer? If split invoices, send an agreed allocation by EOD. If affidavit, please sign the DocuSign envelope and upload a bank confirmation for the receiving account.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Hi Priya / Ben / Soojin,

Finance here. To clear the tax hold and release the December payout we need the following items (pick one path):

Path A (Split invoices - fastest):
- Completed allocation matrix (we received the draft; need your sign-off).
- For each legal entity receiving funds: a PDF invoice in our AP system with matching line-level amounts and the receiving entity legal name.
- Bank details for each receiving entity (bank statement or remittance confirmation).

Path B (Single invoice + reverse-charge affidavit):
- Completed and signed DocuSign affidavit (we started envelope ID ENVELOPE12345RDW).
- GST registration evidence for the supplier (we have the India snapshot; we also need Singapore GST registration screenshot).
- A signed remittance instruction showing the beneficiary account and entity name.

Once we receive either A or B and validate the GST IDs (we run the SG/API check + India GSTIN verification), we will release funds within 24 business hours. Note: if any IDs fail validation we will need additional documentation and that will push the payout beyond the 12/10 window.
